acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Orcs family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Warrior, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Warpaint Breach Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Broad-shouldered with red war paint across the eyes, iron-banded leather, a heavy axe, first ritual scars, and tusks that rise clearly above the lower lip.

Signature mechanic: Red-Line Breach: the Warrior smears fresh paint down one axe cheek, checks forward behind iron-banded leather, then sweeps toward the painted side; the second beat occurs only if the shoulder makes contact.
battlefieldDuty: Maintain reliable line pressure by using an iron-banded shoulder check to open a guard, then occupying the breach with a controlled heavy-axe follow-through.
constructionDimensions: Clan equipment becomes pressure-catching war gear: split-hide standards, vane pauldrons, feathered tusk rings, perforated armor plates, and broad weapon fins preserve heavy iron beneath directional surfaces.

Motion and silhouette emphasize stored force through taut banner cords, flattened fur, dust streamers, pressure dents, and one-way gust channels that extend a committed charge without making the Orc weightless.
counterplay: Dodge to the unpainted side or stop the shoulder before contact; either response cancels the sweep and exposes the Warrior's underarm while the heavy axe resets. Affinity signal: Standards and fur snap flat along the chosen lane before pressure releases; leaving that lane or cutting the loaded banner cord makes the charge overshoot into a long recovery.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only wind treatment without vanes, pressure-catching surfaces, and directional motion
Glow-only wind treatment without readable airflow or stored-force construction
Floating or transparent anatomy that removes the Orc's physical weight
Omnidirectional turbulence that obscures the charge lane
identityInvariants: Tall, broad, top-heavy humanoid silhouette with a thick neck, wide shoulders, heavy jaw, forward lean, and lower tusks rising past the lip.
Grey-green or ash-grey skin is framed by blood red, black, dark iron, bone white, and readable red or white war paint.
Boiled leather, fur, riveted iron, bone, and crude steel remain thick, weighty, and practical rather than elegant or finely matched.
Scars, paint, tusk rings, piercings, skull trophies, spiked pauldrons, and clan totems communicate earned encounter rank without becoming a biological claim.
Tusk length, muscle mass, posture, and carried trophies escalate together, but every form retains committed heavy motion and exposed recovery as the family combat grammar.
telegraph: It drags two fingers through the red band across its eyes, marks one axe cheek, and turns the matching shoulder forward.
